object.title: The near-bipartite characterization conjecture for ${\operatorname{LS}}_+$-perfect graphs
object.statement: For a graph $G$, let $\operatorname{STAB}(G)$ be its stable set polytope, $\operatorname{NB}(G)$ the near-bipartite polyhedral relaxation, and ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)$ the Lovász–Schrijver positive semidefinite relaxation. A polyhedron is **polyhedral** if it can be described by finitely many linear inequalities. **The near-bipartite characterization conjecture.** For every graph $G$, the following four statements are equivalent: (1) $\operatorname{STAB}(G)=\operatorname{NB}(G)$; (2) ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)=\operatorname{STAB}(G)$; (3) ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)=\operatorname{NB}(G)$; and (4) ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)$ is polyhedral. This would characterize the graphs on which the Lovász–Schrijver operator reaches the stable set polytope using the near-bipartite relaxation; the paper presents it as an open conjecture.
object.source_name: S. Bianchi, M. Escalante, G. Nasini and L. Tunçel, “Lovász-Schrijver SDP-operator, near-perfect graphs and near-bipartite graphs”, arXiv:1411.2069 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.2069

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

object.title: Balog's conjecture on the size of $AA+A$
object.statement:
Let $A
e
othing$ be a finite set of positive real numbers, and define

$$
AA+A:=\{ab+c:a,b,c\in A\}.
$$

**Balog's conjecture.** For every such set $A$,

$$
|AA+A|\geq |A|^2.
$$

The conjecture was proposed as an analogue of the Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture. It is refuted by the construction in this paper, which gives arbitrarily large finite sets of rational numbers for which $|AA+A|$ is smaller than $|A|^2$ by a factor involving a power of $\log\log|A|$.
object.source_name: Oliver Roche-Newton, Imre Z. Ruzsa, Chun-Yen Shen and Ilya D. Shkredov, “On the size of the set AA+A”, arXiv:1801.10431 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.10431

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2018); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Andreae's ubiquity conjecture for locally finite connected graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For a graph relation $\vartriangleleft$, say that $G$ is **$\vartriangleleft$-ubiquitous** if, whenever a graph $\Gamma$ satisfies

$$
nG\vartriangleleft\Gamma
$$

for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, it also satisfies

$$
\aleph_0G\vartriangleleft\Gamma,
$$

where $\alpha G$ denotes the disjoint union of $\alpha$ copies of $G$. In particular, let $\preccurlyeq$ denote the minor relation. **Andreae's ubiquity conjecture.** Every locally finite connected graph is $\preccurlyeq$-ubiquitous. This is a central open problem in the theory of infinite graphs; although non-ubiquitous graphs are known for some relations, no simple example is known for the minor relation, and it remains open whether a countable connected graph can fail to be minor-ubiquitous.
object.source_name: Nathan Bowler, Christian Elbracht, Joshua Erde, Pascal Gollin, Karl Heuer, Max Pitz and Maximilian Teegen, “Ubiquity in graphs I: Topological ubiquity of trees”, arXiv:1806.04008 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.04008

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2018).

object.title: Conforti–Cornuéjols integer round-down conjecture
object.statement:
Let ${\mathcal H}$ be a hypergraph with incidence matrix $M$. Say that ${\mathcal H}$ has the **packing property** when every minor of ${\mathcal H}$ is König, and say that $M$ has the **integer round-down property** when

$$
\nu_{\mathbf a}(M)=\left\lfloor\nu^*_{\mathbf a}(M)\right\rfloor
$$

for every ${\mathbf a}\in{\mathbb N}^n$.

**Conforti–Cornuéjols integer round-down conjecture.** If ${\mathcal H}$ has the packing property, then it has the integer round-down property.

The paper states this as an equivalent formulation of the Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Huy Tai Ha and Ngo Viet Trung, “Membership criteria and containments of powers of monomial ideals”, arXiv:1808.05899 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05899

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

object.title: Hanson and Toft's minimum-edge conjecture for Ramsey co-critical graphs
object.statement:
Let $K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_r}$ be complete graphs, let $R=R(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_r})$ be their classical Ramsey number, and let $G$ be a $(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_r})$-co-critical graph on $n$ vertices. The graph $K_{R-2}+\overline{K}_{n-R+2}$ has $(R-2)(n-R+2)+\binom{R-2}{2}$ edges. **Hanson and Toft's conjecture.** Every such graph satisfies

$$
e(G)\ge (R-2)(n-R+2)+\binom{R-2}{2},
$$

with equality attainable for every $n$. Hanson and Toft stated this as the lower-bound counterpart to their sharp upper bound $e(G)\le e(T_{R-1,n})$; the source gives no resolution status for the conjecture.
object.source_name: Zi-Xia Song and Jingmei Zhang, “On the size of (K_t,T_k)-co-critical graphs”, arXiv:1904.07825 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.07825

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

object.title: Erdős's conjecture on sparse Steiner triple systems
object.statement:
For an integer $e\ge 2$, an $(n,3,2)$-design is an $e$-sparse Steiner triple system if it is simultaneously $\mathscr{G}_3(i+2,i)$-free for every $2\le i\le e$. **Erdős's conjecture.** For every fixed integer $e\ge 2$, there exists $n_0=n_0(e)$ such that an $n$-vertex $e$-sparse Steiner triple system exists for every $n\ge n_0$ satisfying

$$
n\equiv 1,3\pmod 6.
$$

The paper reports substantial recent progress, including constructions of $e$-sparse packings, but the stated Steiner-system existence assertion is not presented as fully resolved.
object.source_name: Chong Shangguan and Itzhak Tamo, “Degenerate Turán densities of sparse hypergraphs”, arXiv:1907.04930 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.04930

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2019).

object.title: The Goldberg snark circular-flow-number conjecture
object.statement:
For every positive integer $k$, let $G_{2k+1}$ be the Goldberg snark on $8(2k+1)$ vertices, and let $\Phi_c(G_{2k+1})$ denote its circular flow number. **The Goldberg snark circular-flow-number conjecture.**

$$
\Phi_c(G_{2k+1})=4+\frac{1}{k+1}.
$$

The paper verifies this equality for $G_3$, $G_5$, and $G_7$, while proving the corresponding upper bound for every positive integer $k$. Optimality of that upper bound remains open.
object.source_name: Jan Goedgebeur, Davide Mattiolo and Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo, “An algorithm and new bounds for the circular flow number of snarks”, arXiv:1909.09870 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.09870

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

object.title: Erdős's convex sumset conjecture
object.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a finite **convex set**, meaning that if $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_k\}$, then

$$
a_i-a_{i-1}<a_{i+1}-a_i
$$

for every $1<i<k$. **Erdős's conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$,

$$
|A+A|\gg_{\epsilon}|A|^{2-\epsilon}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the additive growth of convex sets. The paper proves a related lower bound for sums with an arbitrary finite set, but the stated conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Imre Ruzsa, George Shakan, Jozsef Solymosi and Endre Szemerédi, “On distinct consecutive differences”, arXiv:1910.02159 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02159

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

object.title: Universal local Hadwiger conjecture
object.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $t$ be an integer, and for $v\in V(G)$ let $N_G[v]$ denote the closed neighborhood of $v$. **Universal local Hadwiger conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph without a $K_{t+1}$-minor, then $\chi(N_G[v]) \leqslant t$ for all $v \in V(G)$. The source describes this as an apparent weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture that is actually equivalent to Hadwiger's conjecture, so its status is the same as Hadwiger's conjecture and remains open.
object.source_name: Tony Huynh, Bruce Reed, David R. Wood and Liana Yepremyan, “Notes on Tree- and Path-chromatic Number”, arXiv:2002.05363 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05363

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

object.title: Countable-alphabet extension of Proposition valzeroun
object.statement:
Let $X$ be a countable alphabet and let the weak shuffle algebra and the objects in Proposition valzeroun be defined as in the paper. **Countable-alphabet extension.** Proposition valzeroun remains true when the alphabet $X$ is countable.

This extends the preceding result from the setting considered there to arbitrary countable alphabets. The supplied context does not state whether the extension has been proved elsewhere or remains open.
object.source_name: Cécile Mammez, “Weak stuffle algebras”, arXiv:2003.09142 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09142

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

object.title: Robertson's conjecture on bounded Robertson chains
object.statement: Let a **Robertson chain** of length $k$ be the graph obtained from a path of length $k$ by duplicating each edge. A graph contains another graph as a **topological minor** if the latter can be obtained from a subgraph of the former by repeatedly contracting edges incident with vertices of degree two. **Robertson's conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, graphs that do not contain the Robertson chain of length $k$ as a topological minor are well-quasi-ordered by the topological minor relation. This conjecture identifies the known obstruction to well-quasi-ordering graphs under topological containment and is the main objective of the paper; the bounded tree-width case is proved here, while the general conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Chun-Hung Liu and Robin Thomas, “Robertson's conjecture I. Well-quasi-ordering bounded tree-width graphs by the topological minor relation”, arXiv:2006.00192 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.00192

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2020). “This conjecture was proved by Kruskal and independently by Tarkowski in 1960; now it is usually called Kruskal's Tree Theorem.”

object.title: The removal lemma conjecture for Latin squares
object.statement:
Let $k,\ell\in\mathbb N$ and let $A\in\mathcal{R}(k,\ell)$. For a Latin square $L$ of order $n$, write $t(A,L)$ for the density of copies of the pattern $A$ in $L$. If entries are replaced by $*$, define $t(A,L^*)$ so that entries marked with $*$ do not contribute.

**Latin-square removal lemma conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that, whenever $L$ is a Latin square of order $n$ with $t(A,L)<\delta$, at most $\varepsilon n^2$ entries can be replaced by $*$ to obtain a matrix $L^*$ satisfying $t(A,L^*)=0$.

This is the direct analogue of the graph removal lemma, but the resulting object is no longer a Latin square because entries have been deleted. The statement is presented as a conjecture and no resolution is supplied here.
object.source_name: Frederik Garbe, Robert Hancock, Jan Hladký and Maryam Sharifzadeh, “Limits of Latin squares”, arXiv:2010.07854 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07854

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

object.title: Hypergraph Ringel conjecture for $k$-trees
object.statement: Let $k,n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{1\}$. A **$k$-tree** is defined recursively: a single edge is a $k$-tree, and a $k$-tree with $\ell$ edges is obtained from one with $\ell-1$ edges by adding a vertex and an edge containing that vertex and a $(k-1)$-set contained in an existing edge. **Hypergraph Ringel conjecture.** If $T$ is a $k$-tree with $n$ edges, then $K_{kn+k-1}^{(k)}$ admits a decomposition into copies of $T$. This is the proposed $k$-uniform generalisation of Ringel's conjecture; the source notes that the bound is necessary for arbitrary $k$-trees and that the star case is elementary, but the general assertion remains open.
object.source_name: Stefan Ehard and Felix Joos, “Decompositions of quasirandom hypergraphs into hypergraphs of bounded degree”, arXiv:2011.05359 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.05359

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

object.title: Erdős–Graham conjecture for equal-colored variables
object.statement: An equation is **partition regular** if every finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits a solution whose variables all have the same color. **Erdős–Graham conjecture.** For every finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$, there exist $x,y$ of the same color such that $x^2+y^2$ or $x^2-y^2$ is a perfect square. The two-color case for $x^2+y^2$ is known, but the stated finite-coloring problem remains open, including the weaker requirement that only $x$ and $y$ have the same color.
object.source_name: Sebastián Donoso, Anh N. Le, Joel Moreira and Wenbo Sun, “Additive averages of multiplicative correlation sequences and applications”, arXiv:2101.02832 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.02832

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

object.title: The packing problem for hypergraphs
object.statement:
Let $H=(V,E)$ be a hypergraph, and let $I(H)$ be its edge ideal. A **minor** of $H$ is obtained by deleting and contracting vertices. The hypergraph $H$ has the **packing property** if every minor $h$ is König, that is, if its transversal number equals its matching number, $\tau(h)=\pi(h)$. **The packing problem for hypergraphs.** The edge ideal satisfies

$$
I(H)^{(m)}=I(H)^m
$$

for every $m\in\mathbb{N}$ if and only if $H$ has the packing property. This is the combinatorial formulation of the square-free monomial ideal packing problem; its general status is open.
object.source_name: Hrishikesh Bodas, Benjamin Drabkin, Caleb Fong, Su Jin, Justin Kim, Wenxuan Li, Alexandra Seceleanu, Tingting Tang and Brendan Williams, “Consequences of the packing problem”, arXiv:2101.04010 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04010

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

object.title: Las Vergnas–Meyniel conjecture on Kempe equivalence and graph minors
object.statement: For a graph $G$, a **$t$-colouring** is a proper colouring using $t$ colours, and two colourings are **Kempe equivalent** when they are connected by a sequence of Kempe changes, each swapping two colours on a maximal bichromatic component. Let $K_t$ denote the complete graph on $t$ vertices, and say that $G$ has no $K_t$-minor when it does not contain $K_t$ as a graph minor. **Las Vergnas–Meyniel's Conjecture A.** For every $t$, all the $t$-colourings of a graph with no $K_t$-minor form a single equivalence class. The paper states that this conjecture is disproved by its construction of graphs with no $K_t$-minor having non-equivalent colourings.
object.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Marc Heinrich, Clément Legrand-Duchesne and Jonathan Narboni, “On a recolouring version of Hadwiger's conjecture”, arXiv:2103.10684 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10684

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2021); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: The nonchalant-word convergence conjecture
object.statement:
Fix an ordered alphabet $\mathbb A_n=\{\mathtt{1,2,\dots,n}\}$ and let $(N_i)$ be the sequence of nonchalant words produced by the recursive square-free greedy procedure.

**Nonchalant-word convergence conjecture.** The sequence of nonchalant words over $\mathbb A_n$ converges to an infinite word $\mathcal{N}_n$ for every $n\geqslant 3$.

The paper presents this as a plausible strengthening suggested by experiments; no proof or resolution is supplied.
object.source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, Hubert Kordulewski and Bartłomiej Pawlik, “Square-free extensions of words”, arXiv:2104.04841 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04841

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2021).

object.title: Rainbow Erdős matching conjecture
object.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ and let $\binom{[n]}{k}$ denote the collection of all $k$-subsets of $[n]$. Let $\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2,\dots,\mathcal{F}_s\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$. They **contain a rainbow matching** if there exist pairwise disjoint sets $F_i\in\mathcal{F}_i$ for all $1\leq i\leq s$. **Rainbow Erdős matching conjecture.** If

$$
|\mathcal{F}_i|>\max\left\{\binom{ks-1}{k},\binom{n}{k}-\binom{n-s+1}{k}\right\}
$$

for all $1\leq i\leq s$, then $\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2,\dots,\mathcal{F}_s$ contain a rainbow matching. This is a proposed rainbow analogue of the Erdős matching conjecture; the general assertion is not established by the context provided.
object.source_name: Jian Wang and Jie You, “Extremal Problem for Matchings and Rainbow Matchings on Direct Products”, arXiv:2111.04423 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.04423

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2021).

object.title: Odd-minor clustered and defective colouring conjecture
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, let $\mathcal{G}_H^{\text{odd}}$ be the class of graphs with no $H$ odd-minor, let $\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)$ denote the connected tree-depth of $H$, let $\chi_{\star}(\mathcal{G}_H^{\text{odd}})$ be the clustered chromatic number, and let $\chi_{\Delta}(\mathcal{G}_H^{\text{odd}})$ be the defective chromatic number. **Odd-minor clustered and defective colouring conjecture.** For every graph $H$,

$$
\chi_{\star}(\mathcal{G}_H^{\text{odd}})\leqslant 2\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)-2
$$

and

$$
\chi_{\Delta}(\mathcal{G}_H^{\text{odd}})=\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)-1.
$$

The paper proves the weaker upper bound $\chi_{\star}(\mathcal{G}_H^{\text{odd}})\leqslant 3\cdot 2^{\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)}-4$ and places the conjecture as the proposed improvement; its status is not resolved in the source.
object.source_name: Robert Hickingbotham, Dong Yeap Kang, Sang-il Oum, Raphael Steiner and David R. Wood, “Clustered Colouring of Odd-H-Minor-Free Graphs”, arXiv:2308.15721 (2024).
object.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1803.07694](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07694), [arXiv:1708.02370](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02370).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.15721

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2023). “This is one of the most important open problems in graph theory.”

object.title: Strong Hadwiger's conjecture
object.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $[?]{}$ and let $S\subseteq V(G)$ be **colorful** if every proper $\chi(G)$-coloring of $G$ assigns all $\chi(G)$ colors to vertices in $S$. An $S$-rooted $K_t$-minor is a model $(B_i)_{i=1}^{t}$ of $K_t$ in $G$ such that $B_i\cap S\neq\emptyset$ for every $i\in[t]$. **Strong Hadwiger's conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph with $\chi(G)=t$ and $S$ is a colorful set in $G$, then $G$ contains an $S$-rooted $K_t$-minor. This strengthens Hadwiger's conjecture by requiring the complete minor to meet a prescribed set that is hard to avoid in every optimal coloring; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
object.source_name: Anders Martinsson and Raphael Steiner, “Strengthening Hadwiger's conjecture for 4- and 5-chromatic graphs”, arXiv:2209.00594 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.00594

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2022). “Hadwiger's conjecture, among the most famous and difficult open problems in graph theory, states the following.”
